page: Vultr vc2-16c-64gb is a General Purpose cloud server belonging to the Cloud Compute family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.0 GHz. The configuration provides 16 vCPUs mapped from 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled under a shared CPU allocation model. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled with a local 1280 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across most standard workloads. The server achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1451.59 and a multi-core score of 21535.52. Memory bandwidth tests show 107.12 GB/sec for large-block read-only operations and 53.71 GB/sec for write operations. However, a notable tradeoff is its single-threaded gzip compression speed of 23.39 GB/sec, which is categorized as weak. This lower single-threaded performance is also reflected in the shared CPU allocation, which may introduce resource contention under sustained peak loads. Conversely, multi-threaded operations perform adequately, with bzip3 multi-threaded decompression reaching 66.52 GB/sec.

Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and substantial NVMe storage, the vc2-16c-64gb offers reasonable qualitative cost efficiency for resource-dense, non-critical workloads. It is well-suited for static web serving, where it demonstrated a throughput of 12.01 GB/sec, and database operations, scoring 4649.2 on PassMark database tests alongside 23.04 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. It can also support lightweight machine learning tasks, processing 709.16 tokens per second for prompt processing on a small 135M LLM model. It is best utilized for general-purpose applications, development environments, and web serving rather than sustained high-performance compute tasks.

Performance benchmarks place this server in the average tier for most operations, including a PassMark CPU score of 21511.0 and Redis SET throughput of 23.04 million operations per second.
